messages:
customer_success: FYI ACME reported a spike of ~12% 504s during a burst (2026-03-16 ~15:40 UTC). They see timeouts around 30s. Escalating to infra/SRE.
maria: looking at cluster, KEDA did scale but new replicas are failing readiness. Init container 'config-init' is CrashLoopBackOff. Pulling logs now.
devon: can you paste the init logs? sounds like a blocking network call.
maria: kubectl logs -n prod acme-infer-6a2d -c config-init
```
[2026-03-16T15:42:03Z] INFO loading tenant config
[2026-03-16T15:42:04Z] INFO calling billing.validateToken
[2026-03-16T15:42:05Z] WARN billing.validateToken -> 429 Too Many Requests
[2026-03-16T15:42:15Z] ERROR billing validation timeout after 10s
[2026-03-16T15:42:15Z] FATAL startup validation failed -> exit 1
```

aj: who added a sync call to billing in startup path? It should not block readiness.
tara: ScaledObject shows minReplicaCount: 0, cooldownSeconds: 300. KEDA triggers on per-tenant queue metric; big bursts cause large fan-out.
maria: summary: stampede of pods running blocking billing validate -> billing returning 429 under quota -> pods never become Ready -> gateway queues up -> 504s for customer.
billing: we see a burst of validateToken requests from service=acme-config-init yesterday. Quota policy changed last week for service accounts; we're throttling internal calls that used to be unthrottled. We're increasing the internal quota now.
aj: short-term mitigations?
maria: Options: 1) set env BYPASS_BILLING_ON_STARTUP=true for acme deployments so startup uses cached config fallback; 2) temporarily bump KEDA minReplicaCount=2 for heavy-tenant namespaces; 3) bump billing internal quota.
devon: I applied the env patch in prod for the acme namespace:
```
kubectl set env deployment/acme-infer -n prod BYPASS_BILLING_ON_STARTUP=true
kubectl rollout restart deployment/acme-infer -n prod
```
maria: after the patch new pods passed readiness and started serving. Queues drained, 504s reduced to <1%.
oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2026-03-16-XX assigned to maria, devon, billing (sev:P2).
billing: increased internal quota x5 and added client-side exponential backoff jitter for validateToken to avoid thundering herd.
lucas: long-term proposals: - remove sync billing call from init; use stale-while-revalidate cached config - introduce tenant warm-pool (prewarmed replicas for known high-throughput tenants) - smooth KEDA trigger (use 60s moving avg or per-tenant RPS threshold)
aj: devon please open a repro + PR. Repro steps in case someone needs to run locally:
1) set BYPASS_BILLING_ON_STARTUP=false
2) run ./tools/load-generator --tenant acme --burst 250qps --duration 2m
3) watch pods: kubectl get pods -n prod -w
4) kubectl logs -n prod <pod> -c config-init
devon: PR opened to make billing validation async and fall back to cached config on startup, with a 48h ETA for review. GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pulls/8422
tara: created infra ticket to allow configuring warm-pool per-tenant and to tune KEDA query smoothing.
maria: drafting a customer note and internal postmortem. Will include timeline, root cause (billing quota + sync startup call + aggressive KEDA fan-out) and action items.
customer_success: ACME acknowledged the workaround and asked for a formal postmortem and timeline for the permanent fix.

ACTION ITEMS:
- devon: land async startup + cache fallback PR (ETA 48h)
- billing: confirm quota change and update runbook (ETA 4h)
- tara/infra: design warm-pool + KEDA smoothing proposal (next week)
- maria: customer postmortem draft (ETA 24h)

maria: tagging @oncall for visibility. will follow up in INC-2026-03-16-XX. :white_check_mark:
